title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-priya-nair
body:
Quick dump of review notes / follow-ups for PR #2384 - KV cache + batching refactor. Mixed checklist, questions to author, and small patch ideas.

High-level summary:
- Goal: centralize KV cache ownership into CacheManager, add continuous batching hook that can prewarm KV and merge requests more aggressively.
- Files touched: kv_cache.h/cpp, batching_scheduler.cc, request_router.cc, unit tests under tests/kv_cache/*.cc

Sanity checklist (quick pass):
- [ ] Compiles on CI (linux, bazel) - saw one Windows-only macro removed, verify no accidental platform regressions.
- [ ] All existing unit tests pass locally (ran tests/kv_cache/* -> two failures: test_cache_eviction, test_concurrent_writes)
- [ ] New tests cover new behaviors (prewarm, merged-batch semantics)
- [ ] No new public API surface changes (CacheManager is internal)

Notes on design choices (questions for author):
- Why is CacheManager lifetime tied to Router rather than Node worker? If we want KV locality per worker for hot prefixes we may need worker-local caches. Need justification for centralization w.r.t throughput.
- prewarm_async() currently spawns a detached thread on cold miss. This can pile up under load (observed in stress runs). Consider using existing thread-pool or scheduling via worker event loop.
- BatchingScheduler uses a fixed max_merge_window_ms = 5ms. Was this tuned? Add comment with benchmark rationale or expose as config.
- Eviction policy: LRU over keys only, no size accounting for per-key kv value sizes. For long sequences this can bump memory — consider tracking bytes and use bytes-based eviction threshold.

Perf notes from local runs (mini benchmark):
- Baseline (main before PR): 95th latency 38ms for seq=512, batch=8
- With PR (CacheManager centralized, prewarm disabled): 95th latency 32ms -> improvement likely from merged-batch logic
- With prewarm_async enabled: 95th latency 29ms but CPU spikes (thread oversubscription) and occasional GC pauses noted in logs.

Repro & debug tips (commands I used):
- bazel test //tests/kv_cache:all --test_output=errors
- ./benchmarks/kv_batch_bench --model=resnet-style --batch=8 --seq=512 --requests=10000
- sudo perf record -g -- ./bin/serving_runtime --config=local_prewarm.yaml

Specific code comments / suggestions (file: kv_cache.h/cpp):
- Suggest renaming CacheKey::id -> CacheKey::prefix_hash for clarity (search replace).
- In CacheManager::GetOrCreate, avoid double lookup pattern (find then emplace). Use emplace_or_assign or use the iterator returned by insert to avoid two map lookups.
- test_cache_eviction flaky: uses time-based sleep(50ms) assumptions. Replace with deterministic advance of fake clock or inject Clock interface.

BatchingScheduler comments (file: batching_scheduler.cc):
- Merge logic: when two requests have compatible device affinity you merge them even if one has a different max_tokens_left. Need a short comment why safe. Might break correctness if one request expects early termination.
- Consider adding metrics: merged_batches_total, merges_rejected_due_to_affinity, prewarm_requests_total. These will help debug regressions in production.

Request routing (file: request_router.cc):
- Fallback policy: if CacheManager returns stale flag, router still sends to primary model. Add telemetry to record stale->fallback transitions for later analysis.

Unit tests and deterministic behavior:
- Add tests to simulate concurrent GetOrCreate under heavy contention. Use thread helper that deterministically schedules (or run with TSan?)
- test_concurrent_writes: failing due to missing lock around value assignment. Either add fine-grained mutex per-entry or use atomic shared_ptr swap.

Follow-ups / TODOs to track in JIRA: (move to linked artifacts)
- INF-1130: Replace detached thread prewarm with thread-pool scheduling (priority: high)
- INF-1131: Add byte-based eviction and update eviction tests (priority: med)
- INF-1132: Add telemetry metrics for merges and prewarm activity (priority: med)

Small patch suggestions (can be committed in separate PRs):
- Replace sleep-based eviction tests with injected Clock (small patch).
- Switch GetOrCreate to use map::try_emplace to reduce lookup.
- Add metrics counters (prom registry) and wire to Console dashboard (follow-up with observability).

Questions for author review in next PR iteration:
- Can you add a short rationale comment in code for central vs worker-local cache choice?
- Can prewarm use the existing worker pool instead of detached threads? If not, why?
- Are there any memory safety checks for very large KV values? (we should guard against OOM on malicious requests)

Misc notes / scratch ideas (brainstorm):
- Hybrid approach: keep a small worker-local hotset plus a global backing store. Local hotset handles micro-second hits, global store handles cross-worker sharing.
- Opportunistic compression for KV values > 1MB (lz4) to reduce memory and cross-worker transfer costs.
- Add an adaptive merge window: increase merge_window_ms during low qps to improve throughput, shrink under high qps for latency SLOs.

Author action items (clear list):
- [ ] Fix test_concurrent_writes (locking or atomic swap)
- [ ] Replace detached prewarm threads with pool scheduling
- [ ] Add eviction byte accounting and update tests
- [ ] Add basic metrics and one dashboard tile for merged batches
- [ ] Add comment about CacheManager lifetime/design choice

If you want I can take the first two small patches (test fix + try_emplace) and open follow-up PRs. Leaving some specific line comments in GitHub as well.

End of scratchpad dump.
